stem.text: The amount of each gas in the exhaust gases from an internal combustion engine is determined.
The exhaust gases are then passed through the exhaust catalyst, known as a catalytic converter.
Which statements about the effect of the catalytic converter are correct?

items: 2  The amount of carbon dioxide decreases.
3 The amount of carbon monoxide does not change.

explanation.text: A catalytic converter removes oxides of nitrogen and carbon monoxide together: 2CO + 2NO → 2CO<sub>2</sub> + N<sub>2</sub>. It also oxidises unburnt hydrocarbons to CO<sub>2</sub> and H<sub>2</sub>O. So N<sub>2</sub> and CO<sub>2</sub> both increase and CO decreases.

optionAnalysis.text: Only statement 1 is true. CO<sub>2</sub> increases rather than decreases, and CO is removed rather than left unchanged.
NO is reduced to N<sub>2</sub>, so the amount of nitrogen increases. Statements 2 and 3 are both false because CO is oxidised to CO<sub>2</sub>.
Statement 2 is false: oxidising CO and hydrocarbons produces more CO<sub>2</sub>, not less.
Statement 3 is false: removing CO is one of the main jobs of the converter.

reasoningChain: Write the main converter reaction: 2CO + 2NO → 2CO<sub>2</sub> + N<sub>2</sub>.
N<sub>2</sub> is a product, so statement 1 is true.
CO<sub>2</sub> is a product, so it increases: statement 2 is false.
CO is a reactant, so it decreases: statement 3 is false.

inferredMistakes.text: Believing a catalytic converter removes CO<sub>2</sub> because it reduces harmful emissions, and so accepting statement 2.
